en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Stool (Pīṭhavagga) within the Itthivimāna (The Heaven of Women)
13. The First Story of the Daughter-in-law’s Mansion “O deity,
you who stand there with such surpassing beauty;”
Illuminating all directions like a star among the herbs,
by what means do you possess such a complexion?
By what means do you succeed here?
Whatever riches there are that are dear to the mind, they arise for you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your radiance shines in all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she explained the deed whose fruit this is:
"When I was among humans, having become a human being..."
I was a daughter-in-law in my father-in-law’s house.
There I saw a stainless bhikkhu,
serene and untroubled.
With my own hands, full of faith, I gave him a cake;
having given him a portion after portion, I offered it.
I rejoice in the Nandana Grove.
Because of that, my complexion is such as this;
because of that, I am successful here.
And riches arise for me,
whatever is dear to the mind.
I declare this to you, O monk of great power.
"While I was a human being, I performed meritorious deeds;
therefore, my power blazes forth in this way,
and my complexion illuminates all directions."
The Thirteenth: The First Daughter-in-Law’s Mansion.
